explanation: Incomplete penetrance is a phenomenon where a dominant allele does not always lead to the expression of the dominant phenotype in a heterozygote. Many dominant alleles exhibit varying degrees of penetrance. An example of incomplete penetrance is polydactyly, which is characterized by extra digits on the hands, feet, or both. Not everyone who inherits the dominant polydactyly allele will actually develop extra digits.
